summary: TOCTOU Race in Edit Tool Allows File Writes Outside the Workspace
description:
Claude Code validated Edit tool targets using point-in-time pathname and symlink resolution that was not bound to the underlying directory inodes or file descriptors. On macOS, a process running inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox could exploit the resulting time-of-check to time-of-use window by atomically swapping an in-workspace parent directory with a symlink after validation completed, causing the unsandboxed Edit implementation to overwrite an attacker-selected user-writable file outside the workspace. Exploiting this required the ability to run attacker-controlled code inside the sandbox, such as through a malicious repository or dependency script.

summary: Uncontrolled Search Path Enables Arbitrary Code Execution via Malicious Git Executable
description:
Claude Desktop on Windows used `uv_spawn` to execute `git.exe` without specifying an absolute path, causing the process to search the current working directory (CWD) before system directories. An attacker could place a malicious `git.exe` in a project directory (e.g., via a shared git repository), and it would be automatically executed when a user opened that directory in Claude Desktop, without any explicit user interaction beyond opening the project. This constituted a remote code execution vulnerability exploitable through supply chain vectors such as cloned repositories.

summary: Plugin Commit SHA Pin Bypass Allows Installation of Attacker-Controlled Code
description:
The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using `git checkout` without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash. Exploitation required a user to install a malicious plugin, pin to a safe hash, and for the plugin source to be hosted on a git host that permitted SHA-shaped branch names.

summary: Arbitrary File Write via Write-Time Symlink Following (TOCTOU) in Claude Code
description: Claude Code validated that a target file path resided within the project working directory at permission-check time, but re-resolved the path at write time without repeating that validation.
